Read a bounded official BOJ XLS/XLSX workbook

Source: R/workbook.R
read_boj_workbook.Rd

Reads one or more sheets from a local Bank of Japan (BOJ) Excel workbook as text-valued tables. Keeping every cell as text preserves official identifiers, labels, units, and suppression markers. The exact source workbook remains identified by SHA-256 provenance. This is a structural reader: it does not infer a time-series schema from presentation tables, evaluate a publication's definitions, or silently join survey breaks.

Usage

read_boj_workbook(
  path,
  sheets = NULL,
  max_sheets = 100L,
  max_rows_per_sheet = 200000L,
  max_columns = 1000L,
  max_cells = 5000000L
)

Arguments

path

A local regular .xls/.xlsx workbook path, or the length-one boj_file returned by download_boj_tankan_asset(). The file is opened locally; this function does not download it or search the readboj cache.

sheets

Optional non-empty character vector of unique exact sheet names. The default NULL reads every sheet in workbook order. Requested names must exist; no partial or fuzzy matching is performed.

max_sheets

Positive integer maximum number of sheets in the workbook. The default is 100L.

max_rows_per_sheet

Positive integer maximum rows read from each selected sheet. The default is 200000L; one extra row is read to detect an over-limit sheet.

max_columns

Positive integer maximum columns in each selected sheet. The default is 1000L.

max_cells

Positive integer maximum aggregate cells retained across selected sheets. The default is 5000000L.

Value

A named base list, with one element per selected sheet in sheets order (or workbook order from readxl::excel_sheets() when sheets is NULL). Each element is a base data.frame whose column names are repaired to be unique by readxl and whose cells are character values or NA_character_; no numeric or date conversion is performed. The list has a readboj_provenance() attribute containing the source path/hash and byte count (or the downloaded response provenance), parser/schema and package versions, selected sheet names, and aggregate cells count.

Details

The workbook is inspected with readxl using col_types = "text". Sheet count is checked before reading, and row, column, and aggregate-cell bounds are checked while reading. Formula results, merged-cell layout, formatting, hidden sheets, and workbook-specific semantic conventions are not normalised into a BOJ time-series schema; use the returned raw tables and the publication documentation to interpret them.

Reading is local and has no network or cache side effect. readxl may use temporary resources internally, but readboj does not write to the home or a global workspace. A missing/non-regular path, unreadable or malformed workbook, absent/duplicated sheet selection, or any sheet/cell bound violation produces a typed readboj error (readboj_parameter_error, readboj_archive_error, readboj_identity_error, or readboj_size_error).

See also

download_boj_tankan_asset(), list_boj_tankan_assets(), read_boj_bulk(), boj_provenance()

Examples

if (requireNamespace("writexl", quietly = TRUE)) {
  local({
    workbook <- tempfile(fileext = ".xlsx")
    on.exit(unlink(workbook), add = TRUE)
    writexl::write_xlsx(list(catalogue = data.frame(
      series_code = c("SYNTHM01", "SYNTHM02"),
      marker = c("ND", "NA"),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )), workbook)
    tables <- read_boj_workbook(workbook, max_rows_per_sheet = 10L,
      max_columns = 5L, max_cells = 50L)
    tables$catalogue[c("series_code", "marker")]
  })
}
#>   series_code marker
#> 1    SYNTHM01     ND
#> 2    SYNTHM02     NA
